TabVideoOptions: In window mode you can interact with other windows easier. In windowed fullscreen you can quickly switch between applications. In fullscreen we can save memory and render slightly faster.

This is the fastest frame rate that is allowed. Set this lower for a more consistent frame rate or higher for the best experience on faster machines. You may need to disable VSync to reach high frame rates.
These options offer a quick way to dial in the video quality with a single click. Try a few options to see what fits for preference and computer. You can refine further with the options below.
By only rendering nearby objects we can render much faster. Keep in mind seeing further can be an advantage. This can have a strong impact on a slower computer (processor and graphic card).

Shadows can improve the look but they also allow better depth perception. Shadows require all objects to be processed multiple times (processor). Higher quality shadows require more memory and render performance (graphic card).

Textures give flat objects a more detailed appearance. Higher resolution textures can result in crisper images. With more graphic card memory you can choose a higher quality. A lower setting can result in less hitches due to texture streaming. Higher settings are not available on a 32-bit OS.

Various other options contribute to the game look. Most of these options only matter in specific situations. This means the setting might not affect your current image but it can have a large effect later on.

entries.label: Window Mode
entries.tooltip: In window mode you can interact with other windows easier. In windowed fullscreen you can quickly switch between applications. In fullscreen we can save memory and render slightly faster.
entries.wiredTo: Win32: Windowed = overlapped window with the requested client size; WindowedFullscreen = borderless popup over the monitor; Fullscreen = ChangeDisplaySettingsEx(CDS_FULLSCREEN) + popup window (settings::win::apply_display).
entries.note: Mode names are the Fortnite.VideoOptions strings. Default Windowed matches the runtime start-up. Default is ASSUMED: DefaultGameUserSettings.ini / DefaultScalability.ini are encrypted in the pak.

entries.label: Display Resolution
entries.tooltip: In window mode this defines the window size. In windowed fullscreen mode it works similar to the resolution scale. In fullscreen it defines the graphic card output resolution (depending on monitor and graphic card this can result in black borders).

entries.label: Anti-Aliasing
entries.wiredTo: Post pass in post.rs: Off = none, Medium/High/Epic = FXAA (luma edge search, 3.11-style) with increasing sub-pixel strength, edge threshold and search length (settings::aa_params).
entries.note: The level-to-FXAA mapping is an APPROXIMATION: the original uses UE4 post-process AA (sg.PostProcessAAQuality, encrypted DefaultScalability.ini). No MSAA or temporal AA exists in this runtime; FXAA runs on the tone-mapped LDR image. Default Epic = the quality the runtime already renders at. Default is ASSUMED: DefaultGameUserSettings.ini / DefaultScalability.ini are encrypted in the pak.
evidence: label "Anti-Aliasing" present in Game.locres / widget bytecode

entries.label: Textures
entries.tooltip: Textures give flat objects a more detailed appearance. Higher resolution textures can result in crisper images. With more graphic card memory you can choose a higher quality. A lower setting can result in less hitches due to texture streaming. Higher settings are not available on a 32-bit OS.
entries.wiredTo: Mip skip and anisotropy on every texture uploaded through assets.rs (assets::set_texture_quality): Low = skip 2 top mips, Medium = skip 1, High = full mips + 4x anisotropy, Epic = full mips + 16x anisotropy (settings::texture_params).
entries.note: The level mapping is an APPROXIMATION (UE streams a texture pool by sg.TextureQuality; the real per-level mip bias is in the encrypted DefaultScalability.ini). Only textures uploaded through assets.rs are affected (ground, character, pickaxe); the sky textures and the UI are untouched. Default Epic = the quality the runtime already renders at. Default is ASSUMED: DefaultGameUserSettings.ini / DefaultScalability.ini are encrypted in the pak.
